en.body:
For an actor who has navigated the treacherous waters of Hollywood with both blockbuster appeal and a distinct artistic sensibility, **Josh Hartnett** has always possessed a remarkable ability to choose projects that resonate. Now, as he gears up for his role in the upcoming film adaptation of **'Verity,'** Hartnett is looking back at a career filled with memorable collaborations and personal growth.

When asked what drew him to **'Verity,'** Hartnett pointed to the talent involved, specifically praising co-stars **Anne Hathaway** and **Dakota Johnson**, and director **Michael Showalter**. "Michael Showalter is one of those directors who seems to be able to switch genres and do things within each genre that's fresh and somehow geared toward a specific audience in, like, the perfect way," Hartnett shared. He elaborated on Showalter's unique ability to serve the script and genre without ego, a quality Hartnett clearly values. This thoughtful approach to filmmaking promises an exciting new chapter for the actor, who has consistently sought out challenging and engaging material.

Hartnett's filmography is a testament to his eclectic taste. He fondly recalls the experience of working on **Warren Beatty's** ambitious, albeit famously troubled, film **'Town & Country.'** While acknowledging the chaos of that production, it remains a significant memory in his acting journey. Equally important to him is the underappreciated gem **'August,'** a film he holds dear for its artistic merit. His time working with auteurs like **Sofia Coppola** and **Oliver Stone** has undoubtedly shaped his perspective, imbuing him with a deeper understanding of cinematic storytelling and the nuances of performance. These experiences, alongside his joy in making films like **'Lucky Number Slevin,'** highlight a career built on passion and a genuine love for the craft.

## A Career of Bold Choices

Hartnett's career has been marked by deliberate choices, including a notable period where he intentionally stepped away from the Hollywood spotlight in the mid-2000s. This hiatus, coupled with his past reflections on potentially turning down the role of Batman for **Christopher Nolan's** iconic franchise, speaks to a man who prioritizes personal artistic fulfillment over conventional career paths. His willingness to embrace less conventional roles and projects, such as **'Valley of the Gods,'** demonstrates a commitment to exploring diverse storytelling and character archetypes. This thoughtful curation of his roles has allowed him to evolve as an actor, offering audiences a rich tapestry of performances that consistently surprise and engage.

## Fan Anticipation Builds

The news of Hartnett's involvement in **'Verity,'** alongside a stellar cast, has already generated significant buzz among fans worldwide. His ability to connect with audiences, whether through intense dramas or more character-driven pieces, has cemented his status as a respected figure in the film community. The anticipation for **'Verity'** is amplified by Hartnett's own enthusiasm and his reputation for delivering compelling performances. Fans are eager to see how he interprets his role and how his collaboration with **Showalter** and his co-stars will translate to the screen, especially given his past successes with visionary directors.

## What's Next

While specific release details for **'Verity'** have not yet been announced, the film is slated for a 2026 release. Fans can also look forward to Hartnett's upcoming television series, **'Below,'** which is scheduled to premiere around the same time, making it a significant period for the actor's presence on screen. His continued dedication to diverse and engaging projects ensures that audiences will have much to anticipate from **Josh Hartnett** in the coming years.

content_raw: Welcome to The B-Side! Here we talk about movie stars! And sometimes we get to talk to stars about their own B-Sides! Today is a big one for us. The legend Josh Hartnett is on the podcast to talk about his new film Verity and dish on some of his B-Sides, including Town & Country , August , and Valley of the Gods . We chat with Hartnett about his growth as an actor, his memories on the chaotic set of the Warren Beatty-starrer Town & Country , his love for the underseen August , his joy making Lucky Number Slevin , and the luck and stress of having both his big movie ( Verity ) open mere days before his big new show ( Below ).  We make mention of this fascinating Vanity Fair piece from 2001, as well as his intentional disappearance from Hollywood in the mid-2000s. There’s also a brief mention of his potential regret in dismissing a chance at playing Batman for Christopher Nolan early on. Read or listen below and subscribe here . Be sure to give us a follow on Bluesky at @tfsbside.bsky.social . Enjoy! The Film Stage: I feel like over your career, you’ve chosen such an interesting variety of projects. I am just very happy with the result, and I think people who see it will be, too, I hope.
